children: The regulator also approves transactions involving Navi, Aditya Birla Renewables and Adani Energy Solutions

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Friday approved four corporate transactions, including French telecom billionaire Xavier Niel's proposed acquisition of a 16.2 per cent stake in UK-based Vodafone Group PLC for 5.1 billion euros.
The Vodafone transaction is being executed through Vega SAS, a French holding company and subsidiary of Maya SAS, Niel's family investment vehicle.

Under an agreement first announced in July, Vega SAS is acquiring the stake from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC. Upon completion, Vega SAS will become the single largest shareholder in Vodafone Group.

Although Vega SAS does not have direct business operations in India, the transaction required clearance from the Indian competition regulator because of Vodafone's domestic presence through its joint venture, Vodafone Idea.
Under Indian competition laws, global acquisitions that cross specified financial or ownership thresholds require CCI clearance to assess their potential impact on competition in domestic markets.

The investment comes as Vodafone Group undergoes corporate restructuring across its European and African operations. The company has divested its Spanish and Italian businesses and completed a network merger in the UK.
Alongside the Vodafone transaction, the CCI approved three other deals involving companies in the financial technology, renewable energy and power infrastructure sectors.
In the fintech sector, the regulator approved the acquisition of a stake in Navi by MIH Payments Holdings BV.

The acquirer is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of global investment group Prosus NV. It operates as an investment holding vehicle, with its portfolio companies having business operations in India.
Navi Ltd is the holding company of the Navi Group, which offers consumer-facing financial products and services through its subsidiaries via a unified mobile application.
The CCI also approved Aditya Birla Renewables' acquisition of Solenergi Power from Shell Overseas Investment BV.
Solenergi is a Mauritius-registered holding company with strategic interests in several solar and wind power generation entities across India.

In another transaction, the CCI approved Adani Energy Solutions' acquisition of 100 per cent of IntelliSmart Infrastructure from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services.
Adani Energy Solutions and IntelliSmart operate in advanced electricity metering infrastructure. IntelliSmart also deploys smart gas meters.
